scores.reason: Fixed-corpus benchmark that isolates retriever contribution and reports BM25 vs embedding vs agent numbers — directly anchors decision 1 and speaks to decision 3's construction question.
Decomposes agentic gain into retrieval vs utilization and shows search effort is weakly aligned with quality — exactly the mechanism-attribution and premise-testing evidence decisions 2 and 4 need.
The canonical academic-paper-search agent with concrete recall deltas against single-query Google/Scholar baselines plus its own benchmark construction — central to decisions 1, 2 and 3.

Attributes recall@50 gains to a specific bounded citation-graph traversal mechanism and shows it beating open-ended deep-research agents — decision 2's mechanism attribution and a challenge to the premise.

Shows evidence recall collapsing from 84.3% to 21.4% when the per-query-curated corpus is replaced with an independent one — the clearest hit on decision 4 and benchmark-construction inflation (C5, C4).

A recent literature-retrieval agent with baseline comparisons and a multidisciplinary benchmark, but gains are reported for the system as a whole on its own benchmark, so it informs decisions 1-3 without mechanism attribution.
Survey/taxonomy whose benchmark critique bears on decision 3, but it reports no measurements itself; useful framing rather than decision-moving evidence.
Literature-search agent that decomposes citation expansion, reformulation and reranking into explicit operators with measured gains — the closest match to the brief's exact system and decision 2.

Quantifies benchmark-content leakage inflating deep-research agent scores — direct evidence for decision 4 that reported gains can be artifacts of evaluation, and informs contamination controls under C4.

General web-research agent design paper about inertia bias and token cost; the mechanism is not one of the brief's named moves and the gains are not literature-search recall, so it informs no decision the brief names.
